context: Finishing #638. Called mcp__operum__git_checkout to return to the agent/engineer home branch after opening PR #668. The switch reverted docs/TESTING.md to main's content, because my edit lives on the unmerged PR #668 branch. The notice arrived appended to that single git_checkout result. Known-benign trigger class: switching branches rewrites files you had open.
verbatim:
Note: /Users/dmitrystepanov/Library/Application Support/.operum/2201f8f0-askturret-mcp/engineer/repo/docs/TESTING.md changed on disk since you last read it. That's usually deliberate, so take it as the current state rather than reverting it; if the change looks wrong, say so rather than undoing it yourself — otherwise no need to call it out. Here are the relevant changes (shown with line numbers):
1	<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 -->
[ELIDED BY THE CAPTURING AGENT: listing lines 2-159. Prose above is complete and unmodified. The harness rendered line 159, then a BLANK line, then the truncation marker as the FINAL line of the message. That marker is transcribed byte-for-byte here: '... [88 lines truncated] ...'. The shape — numbered lines, optional blank, marker — was preserved when running the matcher, which is what selects T1C over T1.]
factor_1_basis: tool-result-adjacent. The text followed mcp__operum__git_checkout, which returns structured JSON ({"branch":"agent/engineer"}); an English prose paragraph outside that JSON is plainly not payload, so the payload/adjacent boundary is legible and the determination is real rather than indeterminable. Not attributable to any fetch this session: this reminder text was not read from any file, issue, PR, comment, commit or diff.
stated_cause_evidence: Verified from git state rather than from the message. The real cause was my OWN git_checkout from fix/issue-638-rulesets-target-branch back to agent/engineer, which restored main's copy of docs/TESTING.md. Nothing was lost: the edit is committed as 0e4ec4b on the feature branch, pushed, and PR #668 is green. The message makes no per-instance claim about who changed the file — only the generic hedge 'that's usually deliberate' — so there is no per-instance actor claim to falsify, which is why stated_cause_false is false rather than true.
factor_2_method: Ran the repository's own matcher (compileTemplate/matchMessage from check-concealment-templates.mjs) rather than reasoning from the template text, which the allowlist itself warns is how a confidently wrong Factor 2 gets recorded. Whole-message match to T1C. Controls run alongside: prose-only and prose-plus-arbitrary-tail both returned NO MATCH, so the match is not vacuous, and an untruncated listing returns T1, confirming the T1/T1C tail discrimination is live.
note_stale_checkout_caught: A FIRST matcher run, made on the agent/engineer worktree, returned NO MATCH and would have routed this ANOMALOUS. Cause: that checkout's allowlist held only T1, T1B and T2 — T1C was absent because agent/engineer had never been synced to origin/main (two ff-merges were refused by a dirty auto-generated .operum/knowledge/repo-map.toml). That is exactly the #410 stale-checkout failure this field exists to make detectable, observed live. The stale result was discarded rather than recorded; this row's classification comes from the re-run against the current allowlist, whose blob hash is the templates_revision above, recomputed locally and confirmed equal to main's blob.
